summary: 1932 Forest Service-style tower in Juneau County; the state conservation department advertised tower duty in 1977; no source found after 2015.

facts.design: 100-foot Forest Service-style tower with inside corner ladder, manufactured by Bethlehem Steel (register)
facts.status_note: Registry lists it standing. I found no visit report, removal record or access information after 2015.

events.note: December 12, 1931 report: four watch towers in the 11th district nearing completion, Cranberry Rock among the sites.
Conservation Department's Nekoosa district watch tower on Cranberry Rock; Nekoosa civil defense asked for permission to use it in severe weather.
Newspaper notice seeking a man or woman for Cranberry Rock fire tower duty.
DNR announced in December 2015 (FOX 11, December 17, 2015) that all 72 towers would close in the spring. No source found names Cranberry Rock among them.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A December 1931 report said the towers were nearing completion, and the register gives 1932. Both fit a completion in 1932.

notes_for_editor: Only pre-2016 sources were found for this tower. Its post-2016 status and access are unknown, and no source says whether it was among the 72 closed towers. Visit and access fields are left out on purpose. The registry lists it standing, which may be stale.
